question: How many new-mover leads are in Lancaster County?
html:
Lancaster County new-mover leads

The context has no Lancaster County count. The ad plan reports new movers only for the nine-county PA core (about 2,300 arm's-length residential sales a month) and the Jersey Shore (about 1,150). It does not break them out by county (Punctual Pros ad plan).

What the data shows

  • PA core new movers: About 2,300 arm's-length residential sales a month across Lancaster, York, Dauphin, Cumberland, Berks, Lebanon, Franklin, Adams and Perry. The source is county deed records (Punctual Pros ad plan, Oct 6, 2026).
  • Jersey Shore new movers: About 1,150 a month (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • Pre-1980 share: One in three PA core buyers bought a pre-1980 home (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • Assumed mail lead rate: 1.0% per piece. This is deliberately set below ANA prospect response of 4-5% (Punctual Pros ad plan caveats).
  • Lancaster sites: Lancaster (Running Pump Rd) is a confirmed tri-brand site, and competition there is among the densest in the footprint (Punctual Pros market profile, Sep 24, 2026).

Why households are not leads

A deed record is a mailable household. A lead is a household that responds. Under the plan's assumption, Lancaster leads per month (est.) equal Lancaster deed sales × 1.0%. The Lancaster sales count is the missing input.

The 1.0% rate is itself a planning assumption. The week-4 mail read should replace it.

A related signal

Building permits measure a different group. They count new construction, not resale buyers.

Lancaster County, Aug 2026Units
Single-family permits48
Total permits124

(Census building permits, nightly snapshot, fetched Oct 8, 2026)

Do not add these to the deed count. Some new-build buyers will also show up in deed records once they close.

Data that would answer it

  • Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds residential transfers, filtered to arm's-length sales over the trailing 3-12 months. This is the same filter used to build the PA core figure.
  • The mail vendor's actual Lancaster drop count from mail drop 1 in week 2.
  • Responses tracked through ServiceTitan by the unique tracking numbers and QR codes set up in week 1, compared with the 10% new-mover holdout.

Next actions

  1. Ask the data vendor for the county split behind the 2,300-a-month PA core figure. Report Lancaster sales and the pre-1980 share separately.
  2. Tag mail drop 1 by county in ServiceTitan so the week-4 read gives Lancaster booked jobs per piece, not just a core-wide rate.
  3. Replace the 1.0% lead-rate assumption with the observed Lancaster response, net of holdout, at the week-4 read.
  4. Repeat the county split for York and Cumberland. That lets the team compare Lancaster with the growth corridor named as priority 1 in the market profile.
markdown:
# Lancaster County new-mover leads

The context has no Lancaster County count. The ad plan reports new movers only for the nine-county PA core (about 2,300 arm's-length residential sales a month) and the Jersey Shore (about 1,150). It does not break them out by county (Punctual Pros ad plan).

## What the data shows

- **PA core new movers:** About 2,300 arm's-length residential sales a month across Lancaster, York, Dauphin, Cumberland, Berks, Lebanon, Franklin, Adams and Perry. The source is county deed records (Punctual Pros ad plan, Oct 6, 2026).
- **Jersey Shore new movers:** About 1,150 a month (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- **Pre-1980 share:** One in three PA core buyers bought a pre-1980 home (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- **Assumed mail lead rate:** 1.0% per piece. This is deliberately set below ANA prospect response of 4-5% (Punctual Pros ad plan caveats).
- **Lancaster sites:** Lancaster (Running Pump Rd) is a confirmed tri-brand site, and competition there is among the densest in the footprint (Punctual Pros market profile, Sep 24, 2026).

## Why households are not leads

A deed record is a mailable household. A lead is a household that responds. Under the plan's assumption, Lancaster leads per month (est.) equal Lancaster deed sales × 1.0%. The Lancaster sales count is the missing input.

The 1.0% rate is itself a planning assumption. The week-4 mail read should replace it.

## A related signal

Building permits measure a different group. They count new construction, not resale buyers.

| Lancaster County, Aug 2026 | Units |
|---|---|
| Single-family permits | 48 |
| Total permits | 124 |

(Census building permits, nightly snapshot, fetched Oct 8, 2026)

Do not add these to the deed count. Some new-build buyers will also show up in deed records once they close.

## Data that would answer it

- Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds residential transfers, filtered to arm's-length sales over the trailing 3-12 months. This is the same filter used to build the PA core figure.
- The mail vendor's actual Lancaster drop count from mail drop 1 in week 2.
- Responses tracked through ServiceTitan by the unique tracking numbers and QR codes set up in week 1, compared with the 10% new-mover holdout.

## Next actions

1. Ask the data vendor for the county split behind the 2,300-a-month PA core figure. Report Lancaster sales and the pre-1980 share separately.
2. Tag mail drop 1 by county in ServiceTitan so the week-4 read gives Lancaster booked jobs per piece, not just a core-wide rate.
3. Replace the 1.0% lead-rate assumption with the observed Lancaster response, net of holdout, at the week-4 read.
4. Repeat the county split for York and Cumberland. That lets the team compare Lancaster with the growth corridor named as priority 1 in the market profile.
